messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@seacliffcapital.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example
Cc: Seacliff Security Team <security@seacliffcapital.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: concise VM evidence + SLAs for SOC2 book

Hi Jonas,

We're pulling together the security evidence pack for our upcoming SOC 2 readiness review and need a concise vulnerability management (VM) checklist from Redwood we can include in the binder. Specifically Seacliff is asking for the following as a short deliverable (1 page preferred):

- Scan cadence for internal and external assets (type + frequency)
- SLA windows for CVE remediation by severity (critical / high / medium / low)
- Retention policy for scan artifacts and proofs (how long we store/export snapshots)
- A short list of the artifact types you can provide (scan exports, patch manifests, ticket links, signed attestation)

If possible please attach a lightweight checklist/PDF and a single recent scan snapshot we can reference. Our reviewer has limited time so the more concise the better.

Can you get that to us by end of day Monday (4/19)? If it's easier we can take a 20-minute call to walk through.

Thanks,
Asha
Asha Rao
Security Lead, Seacliff Capital
asha.rao@seacliffcapital.com

--

Subject: Re: Request: concise VM evidence + SLAs for SOC2 book

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. 

Short answer: we can deliver a one-page checklist plus a sanitized scan snapshot and a signed attestation PDF by EOD Monday. Below is a compact version we can include in the PDF; I'll attach the one-pager and the sample snapshot in my next message.

Proposed lightweight VM checklist (one-paragraph summary + bullets):
- Scan cadence: external internet-exposed hosts scanned weekly (authenticated external scan where applicable); internal host/infra image scans run nightly for CI-built images and weekly for running instances. Container images are scanned at build time and again pre-deploy.
- CVE remediation SLAs (targeted windows from detection to verified fix): Critical: 7 days (expedited hotfix, test, deploy); High: 30 days; Medium: 90 days; Low: best-effort in quarterly cycles. For internet-facing services where exploitability is confirmed, we escalate criticals to a 48-hour mitigation window.
- Artifact retention: raw scan exports and patch manifests retained for 12 months; condensed compliance snapshots (PDF + manifest) retained for 3 years upon request for audit exports.
- Artifact types we provide: authenticated scan export (JSON/CSV), patch manifest (ticket IDs + PRs), timeline e-mails (triage → remediation), signed attestation letter (PDF), and an anonymized example scan snapshot (zip).
- Proof workflow: we maintain a ticket per remediation with trace to commit/PR and deploy; we can provide ticket links or an exported manifest for each CVE on request.

Logistics: attached are: 1) vm-evidence-checklist.pdf (one pager) and 2) scan-snapshot-202703.zip (sanitized). We'll also prepare redwood-sla-attestation.pdf for signature.

If you want the attestation in DocuSign format, say so and we will circulate.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Security Manager, Redwood Inference
